question: Is there a periodic parent tiling, with labels, all of whose labelled collars lie among the labelled parent collars surviving LAST-BIT-20261108-001B for s = 10101 / 00110, one of them off-law? Its cut would be a periodic plane obeying the decoration's law that is not a pinwheel tiling: a crystal escaping the last one-bit decoration.

public_inputs.law: S1*: the 513 labelled parent collars surviving LAST-BIT-20261108-001B (its survivors.json: 153 non-pinwheel collars and 50 pinwheel collars with labels L(s) does not list; and the 310 labelled keys of L(s) that are core collars), with both handednesses.
public_inputs.candidate periods: For each seed, two patches grown by exhaustive extension to tile distance 2 (LAST-BIT-20261108-001B's labelled growth with move orders shuffled by seeds 0 and 1, 3,000 steps each); translation vectors between two of their tiles with the same shape and label and Euclidean length at most 9 (the seed's short leg is 1), and between complete tiles with the same labelled collar.
public_inputs.lattices: The lattices spanned by two candidate periods with at most 32 tiles per period, ordered by tiles per period and then basis length; the first 120 per seed.
public_inputs.torus growth: torus_lib.torus_grow: growth on the lattice's torus from the seed collar, every tile an orbit stored by a canonical image and its translates over a window three tile diameters wider than the fundamental parallelogram, completing collars with S1* depth first with backtracking (fewest legal moves first), 1,000 steps. A completed torus is a periodic labelled tiling all of whose collars lie in S1*.
public_inputs.check: Every completed torus is checked independently of the growth code: its cell and lattice as a ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A decor_lib plane; every cell collar must be a core collar of the level-one law; and the cut must admit a periodic labelling obeying L(s) on the plane's own lattice (decor_lib.periodic, one level). A torus passing the check is a crystal.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the law, the seeds, the candidate periods, the lattice bound, the budgets or the check after seeing results
Dropping seeds or lattices that complete a torus
primary_observable: Whether some seed completes a torus that passes the check, with its tiles per period.
secondary_observables: Per seed: patches grown, candidate periods, lattices tried, and the torus outcomes (completed, none, budget reached, seed invalid on the torus).
cheapest_meaningful_control: Positive: for the constant decoration 00000 / 11111, with the law Q(L) of its labelled level-one collars and the rhombus lattice's collar as seed, the same steps must complete a torus that passes the same check under that decoration's law (the rhombus crystal, cut once, obeys it). A run whose control fails is not read.
decision_or_followup_rule: If a seed completes a torus that passes the check, the decoration fails: one bit per tile, as a decorated substitution, fails in all 1,024 cases. If none does, the attempt is negative within its candidate periods and budgets, and the coordinator's plan for this case applies: the one-bit line is paused with the case recorded open.
stop_rule: Stop at the declared seeds, patches, candidate periods, lattices and budgets.
nonclaims: Exploratory and non-promotable: the lattices come from patches, not from an exhaustive list of periods, and each torus search is exhaustive only within its budget.
No crystal found does not show that the decoration forces the pinwheel; a non-periodic plane could escape it as well.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing, on the same code: patches at tile distance 3 around four seeds (three move orders each) took 50 to 90 seconds each, held 186 to 191 tiles, and showed 0 to 2 pairs of complete tiles with the same shape, label and labelled collar (one seed gave no patch in any order); no lattice came from them, so the relaxed periods (same shape and label) were added and the distance lowered to 2. For the control, two distance-2 patches gave 2 strict periods spanning exactly the rhombus lattice (a torus of 4 tiles completed in 0.3 seconds) and 87 relaxed periods spanning 665 lattices, the rhombus lattice 25th; 40 torus attempts took 4.5 seconds.
